pr_title: build: fix GLIBC < 2.18 compatible issues and android arm binary loading
pr_body:
- Close https://github.com/swc-project/swc/issues/1723
- Close https://github.com/swc-project/swc/issues/3198

### Note
- `rust-toolchain` is upgraded to `nightly-2022-01-19` to avoid `aarch64-linux` cross compile issue.
- `swc_cli` is built as `linux-aarch64-musl` in `linux-aarch64-gnu` build step. Because `musl` executable binary is also works in `gnu` platform.
pr_comments: Seems to be still blocked by https://github.com/swc-project/swc/pull/3196#discussion_r778537610
Semes like `STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN` is not fixed yet? https://github.com/swc-project/swc/runs/4877028875?check_suite_focus=true
I'll try to fix it. It's randomly appeared before. We should adjust some LTO options for Windows arm64 to let the linker consume less memory.

Ah, thank you!
I tried downgrading `rustc`, but it didn't work. Can you please bump it again with the PR for fix?

> I tried downgrading rustc, but it didn't work. 

Seems like it is just because our project is too large for a `7GB RAM` machine to build.

issue_context.title: Issue running on Oracle Linux
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Running @swc-node/jest on Jenkins that is using Oracle Linux. When running I am receiving 

`TypeError: Can not find node binding files from @swc/core-linux-x64-gnu, @swc/core-linux-x64-gnux32, @swc/core-linux-x64-musl and /mnt/jenkins_workspace/ianow_Panda_panda-ssr_master/node_modules/@swc/core/swc.linux-x64-gnu.node, /mnt/jenkins_workspace/ianow_Panda_panda-ssr_master/node_modules/@swc/core/swc.linux-x64-gnux32.node, /mnt/jenkins_workspace/ianow_Panda_panda-ssr_master/node_modules/@swc/core/swc.linux-x64-musl.node`

I see the modules being installed under node_modules/@swc/ but it appears it is looking for it under node_modules/@swc/core/?

**Input code**

**Config**

```javascript
export default {
  resolver: 'jest-ts-webcompat-resolver',
  testMatch: ['**/test/**/*.+(ts)'],
  testPathIgnorePatterns: ['test/MockStore.ts'],
  transform: {
    [`(${esModules}).+\\.js$`]: ['@swc-node/jest'],
    '^.+\\.(ts|tsx)$': ['@swc-node/jest'],
  },
  transformIgnorePatterns: [`/node_modules/(?!${esModules})`],
};
```

```json
{
  "jsc": {
    "parser": {
      "decorators": true,
      "dynamicImport": true,
      "syntax": "typescript",
      "tsx": true
    },
    "target": "es2020"
  }
}
```

**Expected behavior**
Tests to run by finding the correct node bindings.

**Version**
"@swc-node/jest": "^1.2.1",
"@swc/cli": "^0.1.40",
"@swc/core": "^1.2.57",

**Additional context**
Here is the output of the os that the build is running on

- core

cc @Brooooooklyn 
Do you have any idea?
Seems like to be `Glibc` compatible problem again,I will add more useful information in `@node-rs/helper` later.
@SomethingSexy Could you run `ldd --version` on your server, and paste the output?
I am reading the Rust documentation right now, we might need to upgrade our version of glibc? Not sure 2.17 is supported?
`Glibc` is distributed with the operation system, I found a disussion about how to upgrade `Glibc` version on `Oracle linux`: https://access.redhat.com/discussions/3244811
@Brooooooklyn thanks! I will see about getting it upgraded and see if that helps.
@Brooooooklyn  do you know what the minimum version is we should strive to support?
swc will always support the `node:lts` docker image, and the `Glibc` version in it is `2.24` for now
This closed issue has been automatically locked because it had no new activity for a month. If you are running into a similar issue, please create a new issue with the steps to reproduce. Thank you.
